analysis.title: GS Sector Specialists: U.S. Industrials & Materials, breadth A&D into Q3, DAL RPM (Ryan Novak, 5 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Overnight geopolitics per the desk: Bolsonaro took a surprise lead in the first round of Brazil's presidential election, and Brazilian markets are well bid. Spain's PM called a snap election for late November, and the Euro is at 17-month lows. France is in the background, with the market still looking for French candidates with a credible path to fiscal sustainability.

Market snapshot: S&P futures are roughly flat. Japan is up 240bps, KOSPI is modestly higher, and Europe is weaker, led down by France off 105bps. WTI is $91, Brent $102, the 10-year is 5.28% (very modestly off highs), DXY is $102 and Bitcoin is $86k. ISM Services is due later this morning.

Aerospace sentiment into Q3: aerospace used to be a buy-the-dip sector because growth was viewed as largely macro agnostic. The desk says the market has become much more stock specific than thematic. Stocks are trading like March/April (higher jet fuel, fears of a global travel slowdown), but the Middle East conflict is now 7-8 months old and jet fuel is still elevated.

The desk argues that maintenance decisions had no time to adjust in March, but now time is working against the growth outlook. Investors wanted to be long original equipment (BA and the supply chain), but that has proven frustrating given the issues tempering enthusiasm.

Aerospace positioning per the desk: more owned are BA, RBC, CRS, ATI and DPC, with investors warming to HONA on valuation. More debated are WWD (needs to guide) and HWM (CPP deal debate). Underowned are TDG, HEI and TXT.

Defense primes: there is widespread confusion over why the primes have acted poorly even during risk-off and geopolitical escalation. A potential midterm blue wave is a clear overhang, and the desk believes SPCX lock-ups add pressure. Investors are more positive on LMT and GD, mixed on RTX, and more negative on NOC and LHX. Fed IT remains a source of funds, with debate over whether DOGE-related concerns could reaccelerate.

Other US industrials color: SU FP is down 10% on a $24bn acquisition of PTC. Equipment rental names have positive Q3 checks on better time utilization, extending lead times and rates up quarter over quarter. BA has incrementally positive headlines, with the software glitch not viewed as a safety issue.

GS Economics on Q3 earnings: the season kicks off the week of October 12, and about 70% of S&P 500 market cap reports by the end of October. Consensus expects 27% y/y S&P 500 EPS growth, versus realized 33% in Q2 excluding some accounting distortions. AI infrastructure beneficiaries account for over 50% of EPS growth, alongside hyperscaler capex growth of 116%.

GS Economics expects most companies to beat consensus again. Median-stock EPS growth is expected to slow from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3. Input costs likely limit sequential margin expansion, and the dollar is a modestly smaller tailwind to revenue growth. Recent economic growth data have been strong and earnings revision breadth remains positive.

DAL reports Friday Oct 9 pre-market at 6:30am (call at 10am) with a 6% implied move. The stock has been more green than red but moves were muted in the last four quarters. The desk expects a full-year guide update with an implied Q4. Revenue trends are strong to better across airlines, while cost trends are worse both including and excluding fuel.

DAL is more protected than peers given better margins and owning Trainer, which has pushed the stock to relative highs and set an elevated bar. Full-year guidance is $6.50-7.50 EPS and $3-4bn free cash flow. The Street is at $5.89 EPS, below the low end, with Q4 topline growth expected to accelerate to +17% y/y.

RPM reports Tuesday pre-market around 6:45am (call at 10am) with a 4% implied move. It is fiscal Q1, so there may be fewer full-year updates. The stock has been consistently green when reporting fiscal Q1 in recent years, and valuation suggests very low sentiment. 2027 EBITDA consensus sits at the midpoint of the +5-10% guide. The desk looks for topline color across CPG, PCG and Consumer, with potential cost-side headwinds building.
